public_payload.normalized_proposition: If an American AI company is partly owned by the US government, nobody is going to trust it.
conditions: if an American AI company is partly owned by the US government

statement.excerpt: As I noted on X, nobody is going to trust an American AI company that is partly owned by the US Government.

from_speaker: partly owned by the US Government
Just the way the US doesn’t trust Huawei
our_interpretation: The surrounding passage concerns foreign governments and enterprises trusting American AI developers, particularly in Europe and Asia.
I read 'nobody' as a prediction of broad foreign rejection, rather than a literal assertion about every individual.
Partial ownership means an actual US government equity holding. Discussions, procurement contracts, regulation and private charitable funds do not establish that condition.
The relevant companies are AI developers like those named in the passage. Treating every semiconductor supplier as an AI company would broaden the claim beyond its context.
The speaker supplies no deadline or numerical trust measure.
criteria.support_condition: Following a verified government equity acquisition, evidence shows broad foreign restrictions, abandonment or refusal to adopt the affected developer's products because of that ownership, comparable in character to the Huawei analogy.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Following a verified acquisition, substantial foreign government and enterprise adoption or renewal, accompanied by explicit acceptance of the ownership arrangement, demonstrates that broad foreign trust persists.
